messages:
jeff: Heads-up: the docs team is rolling out a samples policy change next week. From Monday samples will default to using ephemeral sandbox keys and the docs previewer will validate request shapes instead of hitting prod/staging.

maria: Will external contributors notice anything when they copy-paste quickstarts?

jeff: We kept backwards compatibility for copy-paste. The migration updates the snippet metadata to include `runner: sandbox` and adds a `vars` entry for the key. Example header the migration inserts: <!-- redwood:example {"language":"py","runner":"sandbox","vars":{"API_KEY":"${{REDACT}}"}} -->

anya: Where's the migration script? can it run across multiple repo READMEs?

jeff: Tool is at repos/docs-tools/sandbox-migrate. It supports dry-run and will back up changed files. Usage: `python -m redwood_docs.sandbox_migrate --path docs/ --dry-run` then `--apply --backup` when ready. It will only touch fenced snippet blocks and README-like files.

maria: CI changes? some of our preview tests currently call staging endpoints.

jeff: Docs CI will get a `REDWOOD_SANDBOX=true` job that spins the mock and runs the previewer. Teams that need live integration can opt into `DOCS_INTEGRATION=true`. We'll publish a migration checklist in the docs repo.

anya: SDK changes required?

jeff: Minimal: we added `redwood-docs-client` helpers in JS/Py/Go that swap endpoints when sandbox=true. Patch releases for samples will be published tomorrow.

docs-bot: Policy: https://git.redwood.example/docs/policies/sandbox-keys.md · migration tool: https://git.redwood.example/docs-tools/pkgs/sandbox-migrate. Run dry-run first.

maria: Thanks. I'll run the tool on integrations/ and open PRs. Tagging owners.

jeff: If you hit multi-file examples or live shell sessions, ping me and we'll schedule a quick triage. :white_check_mark:
